question: Which speakers tend to lead a new change in how a language sounds, often by about a generation?
answer: Young women. Reviewing decades of studies of changing vowels in cities across the English-speaking world, William Labov found women ahead of men in most changes in progress, often by around a generation. The habits mocked in teenage girls, from new vowels to new slang, are frequently the ordinary speech of their grandchildren.
move: Before mocking how the young talk, ask whose speech it will become.
ask: Which new habit in young people do I mock that I may be using myself in ten years?
source: Labov, Principles of Linguistic Change, Vol. 2, 2001
reference: Labov, Principles of Linguistic Change, Volume 2: Social Factors, Blackwell, 2001
